title: A general-purpose allocator
hints: Write three private helpers first and use them everywhere: `read(offset)` and `write(offset, header)` with `std::memcpy`, and `next(offset)` = offset + 16 + that block's payload. Every operation is then a walk `for (at = 0; at < size; at = next(at))`.

To merge with the block before, you need its offset: walk from the start remembering the last block before yours. Merge with the block after first; then, if the previous block is free, grow it to swallow yours (which may already include the next one).
requirements: Headers live inside the region; every returned pointer is 16-aligned.
First fit with splitting when the leftover can hold a block.
Freeing merges with free neighbours on both sides.
Running out returns `nullptr`; freeing everything restores one free block.
stretch: Add `reallocate(p, bytes)` that grows a block in place when the block after it is free and large enough, and only moves it otherwise, the way `realloc` does.
